name: Yellow Rust (Stripe Rust) in Wheat
symptoms: Bright yellow pustules forming parallel narrow stripes along leaf veins. Dust rubs off on fingers as yellow powder. Thrives in cool (10-15°C) and moist/humid weather.
management: Consult KVK / local agricultural officer immediately. Propiconazole 25% EC (1 ml/litre) or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC is commonly recommended by universities upon initial detection at ETL. Spray on calm days.
precautions: Do not delay spraying once stripes are seen. Grow resistant varieties like HD-2967, HD-3086, DBW-187, DBW-222.

name: Leaf Blast in Rice
symptoms: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped lesions with ash-grey centers and brownish-red borders on leaves. Lesions coalesce and kill the leaf blade.
management: Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer application. Recommended treatments include Tricyclazole 75% WP (0.6 g/litre) or Isoprothiolane 40% EC at first appearance.
precautions: Drain standing water temporarily and maintain balanced potassium nutrition.

name: Aphids in Mustard
symptoms: Tiny green or brown soft-bodied insects clustering in large colonies on growing tips, flowers, and developing pods. Excrete sticky honeydew causing sooty mold.
management: Early sowing before Oct 20 reduces infestation. For biological control, encourage ladybird beetles. For chemical control at ETL (15-20 aphids/plant), Dimethoate 30% EC or Thiamethoxam 25% WG under KVK guidance.
precautions: Spray during late afternoon to protect honeybee pollinators.

name: Late Blight in Potato and Tomato
symptoms: Water-soaked irregular blackish-brown spots on leaf tips and margins. White cottony fungal growth visible on underside of leaves in morning under high humidity (>90%) and cool weather (12-18°C).
management: Prophylactic spray of Mancozeb 75% WP (2-2.5 g/litre) before disease onset. After symptoms appear, systemic fungicides like Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (2 g/litre) or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb.
precautions: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; burn or bury infected haulms.

name: Fall Armyworm in Maize
symptoms: Pinholes in young leaves, skeletonized leaf whorls, large chunks eaten, accompanied by coarse brown fecal pellets (frass) inside leaf whorls.
management: Apply dry sand or neem cake (5 g/plant) inside whorls in early stages. Biological: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) or Metarhizium anisopliae. Chemical: Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG (0.4 g/litre) or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC directed into the whorl.
